claims.text: The rider's claim is that a short hop became 4.04 km and $9.70. The governing distance figure is the trace, not the rounded trip-record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 4.04 km against a booked optimal of 3.2 km, an excess of 0.84 km, which is 26.25% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests therefore pass — the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms — so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and discharges it: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02844 and the trace runs from the recorded trip_started event at 11:36:04 to trip_completed at 11:43:34, so the artifacts describe the same trip; and the excess of 0.84 km / 26.25% meets the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from a trace that is unimpaired (100.0% coverage, 46 fixes, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0). The burden now shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

The driver's only explanation on file is 'One-way streets.' That is a general assertion of traffic conditions, unsupported by any traffic_advisory ID, and under POL-RD-08 it does not discharge the driver's burden. It also fails POL-RD-03 on its face: exoneration requires an advisory record naming a road or segment the optimal route traverses with an overlapping validity window, and no such record exists.

No traffic advisory covers this trip at all: EV-ADVIS-02844-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and the note 'No advisory covers the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window.' Under POL-RD-13 the driver's external-traffic assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else; with no advisory on file that comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight. The deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any of this excess. The chat log for this trip is empty — message_count 0, no messages, first_message_at null — so there is no rider instruction meeting POL-RD-04(a) to (c), no waypoint_hint to corroborate, and no distance to exclude. The driver cannot invoke POL-RD-04 on this record.

No relocation of the pickup or dropoff point rescues the driver either. The trip_record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, original_pickup and original_dropoff both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked optimal of 3.2 km stands as the baseline.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, which applies because fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 3.2 + 0.28 x 6.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting time - 0 promo = 8.68. Refund = charged_total 9.70 - 8.68 = 1.02, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 1.05 once rounded up to the nearest 0.05. The surge multiplier was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is 1.0.

The rider should not be left paying for gantries or surcharges he never crossed. The fare_breakdown carries no ERP lines at all (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.0, off_optimal_route_total 0.00) and no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.0), and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no pass-through correction to add and nothing to double-count against the POL-RD-02 figure.

The driver's profile does not aggravate this case, and I do not overstate it: deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 82, which is neither 3 or more flags nor a ratio of 0.05 or more, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06 and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows. The rider's own profile is likewise clean on the citable counters (deviation_claims_60d 0, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0), so the POL-RD-08 corroboration overlay for repeat claimants is not engaged.

The trace is clean for policy purposes as well as for the pre-pass: 46 fixes at a 10 s sample interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires, the deviation may be established on the trace alone, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is triggered. The rider's case does not depend on any impaired artifact.

claims.text: The rider's claim is that a short hop became 4.04 km and $9.70. The governing distance measurement is the GPS trace polyline, not the rounded trip_record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 4.04 km against a booked optimal of 3.2 km, an excess of 0.84 km. That excess is 26.25% of optimal, which clears the 20% limb of POL-RD-01, and 0.84 km clears the 0.8 km absolute limb. Both establishment tests pass, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 46 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so no limb of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires. The deviation therefore stands on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration, and the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) and (b) is discharged: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02844 and the pickup timestamp 2026-08-26T11:36:04+08:00 matches across the trace's first fix and the trip record's trip_started event.

The driver's only explanation on file is 'One-way streets.' That is a general assertion of traffic conditions with no traffic_advisory ID behind it, and POL-RD-08 provides that such an assertion does not discharge the driver's burden. It is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and the bundle's only advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0 - no advisory covers the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window - so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the excuse carries no weight. The driver cited no advisory identifier, so this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged.

No exculpatory clause on the driver's side can run on this record. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction in the chat_log, and the chat log for this trip carries 0 messages with first and last message timestamps null, so there is no instruction to corroborate and no waypoint_hint to test. POL-RD-05 requires an amendment timestamp or an amended optimal, and trip_record.pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null. POL-RD-12 does not apply because vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL. The excess is therefore unexcused in full.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, and the fare model is METERED so that clause governs rather than POL-RD-11. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 3.2 + 0.28 x 6.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 3.80 + 2.40 + 1.68 + 0.80 = 8.68. Charged_total is 9.70, so the refund is 9.70 - 8.68 = 1.02, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is 1.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 1.05. The surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, not from the trip record.

The driver's profile does not rescue him and does not need to be stretched against him. POL-RD-06 is consulted because POL-RD-01 records a deviation, but the deviation is 26.25% excess, which is above the 20% establishment threshold and below the 50% material threshold, so it is not a MATERIAL deviation and the POL-RD-06 pattern test is not triggered. Even if it were, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 247 - a ratio of 0.004, far below the 0.05 limb and below the 3-flag limb - so no pattern is established and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows. I note for completeness that driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 names.

The rider's profile is likewise context only and cuts neither way here. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift for a serial claimant does not apply and the rider's claim needs nothing beyond the trace. No other rider profile field is cited as a ground of decision.

On the pass-through lines, the fare breakdown carries zero ERP gantries and zero tolls, and the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no off-route ERP to refund and no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4). The rider's recovery is confined to the distance and time refund computed under POL-RD-02, and no ERP amount may be added on top of it.

I concede one point against my side: the driver's trace shows a maximum distance from the pickup of 2566 m and a mean of 1353 m, and the trip completed normally at the recorded drop-off with no cancellation and no safety or complaint flag. Nothing in the record suggests the driver abandoned the route or failed to deliver the rider, and I do not argue otherwise. That concession does not touch the arithmetic: the excess is measured and unexcused, and the refund stands at SGD 1.05.

ruling.explanation:
This is a route-deviation dispute over a SGD 9.70 metered fare. Both sides' surviving claims agree on the substance, and the arithmetic is as follows.

Deviation established (POL-RD-01). The governing distance is the GPS trace, not the rounded trip-record copy. trace_distance_km = 4.04 km (EV-GPS-02844) against optimal_distance_km = 3.2 km (EV-TRIP-02844) gives an excess of 0.84 km, which is 26.25% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass — the excess exceeds 20% of optimal and exceeds 0.8 km in absolute terms. The trace figure is essential here: trip_record.actual_distance_km is 4.0 km, which would give exactly 0.8 km and fail the absolute limb, so the trace is the only safe basis for the finding.

Trace integrity (POL-RD-07). The trace is NOT impaired for policy purposes: 46 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0. None of limbs (a) to (c) fires, so the deviation stands on the trace alone, no independent corroboration is required under POL-RD-07(ii), and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises.

The driver's explanation. The only driver explanation on file is the counterparty statement 'One-way streets.' No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-02844-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and the note that no advisory covers the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against this trip's traffic_advisory and nothing else; with no advisory on file that comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver named no advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and no escalation follows.

Driver-side exculpations (POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-12). The chat log (EV-CHAT-02844) carries 0 messages with null timestamps, so there is no rider instruction and no waypoint_hint to test; pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run; vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply. No part of the excess is excluded.

Refund (POL-RD-02). The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 governs rather than POL-RD-11. recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 × 3.2 km + 0.28 × 6.0 min) × 1.0 surge, read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting time − 0.00 promo = 8.68. Refund = charged_total 9.70 − recomputed_fare 8.68 = 1.02, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = SGD 1.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share (8.73), so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 1.05.

Pass-throughs (POL-RD-09). The fare breakdown carries no ERP lines (on-optimal-route and off-optimal-route totals both 0.00) and no airport surcharge, on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport. There is nothing to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure and no billing-integrity finding, so no POL-RD-09(4) referral.

Profiles (POL-RD-06, POL-RD-08, POL-GEN-01). The deviation is 26.25%, above the establishment threshold but below the 50% material threshold, so it is not a MATERIAL deviation and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral arises. No repeat-deviation pattern exists in any event: deviation_flags_90d = 1 against completed_trips_90d = 247, a ratio of 0.004, below both the 3-flag and 0.05 limbs. (One rider submission gave completed_trips_90d as 82; 82 is the 30-day figure on EV-DPROF-02844 — the 90-day figure is 247, and the pattern test fails on either figure, so nothing turns on the slip.) The rider's citable counters, deviation_claims_60d and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated, are both 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration overlay is not engaged. No profile field was used as a ground of decision.

Confidence and escalation. ledger.claim: No rider-requested detour can excuse any of this excess. The chat log for this trip is empty — message_count 0, no messages, first_message_at null — so there is no rider instruction meeting POL-RD-04(a) to (c), no waypoint_hint to corroborate, and no distance to exclude. The driver cannot invoke POL-RD-04 on this record.

No relocation of the pickup or dropoff point rescues the driver either. The trip_record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, original_pickup and original_dropoff both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked optimal of 3.2 km stands as the baseline.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, which applies because fare_breakdown.fare_model is METERED. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 3.2 + 0.28 x 6.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0 ERP + 0 fixed surcharges + 0 waiting time - 0 promo = 8.68. Refund = charged_total 9.70 - 8.68 = 1.02, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and well below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 1.05 once rounded up to the nearest 0.05. The surge multiplier was read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which is 1.0.

The rider should not be left paying for gantries or surcharges he never crossed. The fare_breakdown carries no ERP lines at all (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.0, off_optimal_route_total 0.00) and no airport surcharge (airport_surcharge 0.0), and the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no pass-through correction to add and nothing to double-count against the POL-RD-02 figure.

The driver's profile does not aggravate this case, and I do not overstate it: deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 82, which is neither 3 or more flags nor a ratio of 0.05 or more, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established under POL-RD-06 and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows. The rider's own profile is likewise clean on the citable counters (deviation_claims_60d 0, deviation_claims_60d_substantiated 0), so the POL-RD-08 corroboration overlay for repeat claimants is not engaged.

The trace is clean for policy purposes as well as for the pre-pass: 46 fixes at a 10 s sample interval, 100.0% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires, the deviation may be established on the trace alone, and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation is triggered. The rider's case does not depend on any impaired artifact.

The rider's claim is that a short hop became 4.04 km and $9.70. The governing distance measurement is the GPS trace polyline, not the rounded trip_record copy: gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 4.04 km against a booked optimal of 3.2 km, an excess of 0.84 km. That excess is 26.25% of optimal, which clears the 20% limb of POL-RD-01, and 0.84 km clears the 0.8 km absolute limb. Both establishment tests pass, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 46 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so no limb of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires. The deviation therefore stands on the trace alone and needs no independent corroboration, and the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) and (b) is discharged: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02844 and the pickup timestamp 2026-08-26T11:36:04+08:00 matches across the trace's first fix and the trip record's trip_started event.

The driver's only explanation on file is 'One-way streets.' That is a general assertion of traffic conditions with no traffic_advisory ID behind it, and POL-RD-08 provides that such an assertion does not discharge the driver's burden. It is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, and the bundle's only advisory artifact is MISSING with weight 0.0 - no advisory covers the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window - so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the excuse carries no weight. The driver cited no advisory identifier, so this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged.

ledger.claim: No exculpatory clause on the driver's side can run on this record. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction in the chat_log, and the chat log for this trip carries 0 messages with first and last message timestamps null, so there is no instruction to corroborate and no waypoint_hint to test. POL-RD-05 requires an amendment timestamp or an amended optimal, and trip_record.pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null. POL-RD-12 does not apply because vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL. The excess is therefore unexcused in full.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, and the fare model is METERED so that clause governs rather than POL-RD-11. recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 3.2 + 0.28 x 6.0) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 fixed surcharges + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 3.80 + 2.40 + 1.68 + 0.80 = 8.68. Charged_total is 9.70, so the refund is 9.70 - 8.68 = 1.02, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, which is 1.05. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 1.05. The surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, not from the trip record.

The driver's profile does not rescue him and does not need to be stretched against him. POL-RD-06 is consulted because POL-RD-01 records a deviation, but the deviation is 26.25% excess, which is above the 20% establishment threshold and below the 50% material threshold, so it is not a MATERIAL deviation and the POL-RD-06 pattern test is not triggered. Even if it were, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 247 - a ratio of 0.004, far below the 0.05 limb and below the 3-flag limb - so no pattern is established and no FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral follows. I note for completeness that driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is not the trailing-90-day figure POL-RD-06 names.

ledger.claim: The rider's profile is likewise context only and cuts neither way here. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the POL-RD-08 corroboration uplift for a serial claimant does not apply and the rider's claim needs nothing beyond the trace. No other rider profile field is cited as a ground of decision.

On the pass-through lines, the fare breakdown carries zero ERP gantries and zero tolls, and the airport surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, so there is no off-route ERP to refund and no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4). The rider's recovery is confined to the distance and time refund computed under POL-RD-02, and no ERP amount may be added on top of it.

I concede one point against my side: the driver's trace shows a maximum distance from the pickup of 2566 m and a mean of 1353 m, and the trip completed normally at the recorded drop-off with no cancellation and no safety or complaint flag. Nothing in the record suggests the driver abandoned the route or failed to deliver the rider, and I do not argue otherwise. That concession does not touch the arithmetic: the excess is measured and unexcused, and the refund stands at SGD 1.05.
